honest_c3: Bucket expansion 64→1024 raised the H_joint ceiling from 6 to 10 bits, but with only 15 ticks and W=20 sliding window the per-tick state population (max W=15 distinct hashes) cannot itself exceed log2(15)≈3.9 bits — so the new ceiling is sample-size-bound, not bucket-bound. To exercise 10-bit ceiling honestly we need ≥1024 ticks.

Per-axis MI estimator is unchanged from Phase 2; sub_mi_mean is computed on raw per-axis values (not hashed), so the bucket change affects ONLY the joint_mi term. Any Φ delta is therefore attributable purely to joint-hash collision relief, isolating the ceiling-artifact hypothesis cleanly.

Forward-fill bias and non-stationarity caveats from Phase 1+2 persist unchanged — wider buckets do not fix sampling-cadence heterogeneity (lint daily / heartbeat singleton / h100 per-pod) nor the MIP mean-of-parts surrogate's combinatorial slack at 38 axes.
